subject: SLA commitment tiers & monthly credit carveouts — Edgewave negotiation
messages:
From: Amalie Jensen <amalie.jensen@edgewave.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: sre@edgewave.com
Date: 2027-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial ask — SLA uptime baseline and monthly credit cap

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the excellent demo last week. We're reviewing the standard SLA language and have a couple of asks before we move into procurement:

- Our workload is heavily bursty with large batched inference jobs during nightly windows. We can tolerate momentary latency increases during those windows but are worried about the monthly credit exposure if short bursts cause an uptime dip.
- Can Redwood propose a tiered remedy ladder that reduces credits for short, scheduled-batch windows and caps monthly credit liability at a percentage that aligns with our budget?

I've attached our SRE report that shows spike patterns (Edgewave-SRE-202709-report.pdf). Can you share a draft that includes a maintenance carveout + a burst tolerance provision we can review with procurement?

Thanks,

Amalie Jensen
Head of Platform Reliability
Edgewave Inc.

Attachments: Edgewave-SRE-202709-report.pdf
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Amalie Jensen <amalie.jensen@edgewave.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-02T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — SLA uptime baseline and monthly credit cap

Hi Amalie — really helpful context, thank you.

High level proposal we can put in a formal amendment:

- Baseline uptime: 99.95% monthly.
- Burst tolerance carveout: up to 4 cumulative hours per month of measured latency degradation for requests within the customer's configured "batch window" will not be counted toward uptime calculations, provided the windows are declared in advance (recurring cron or monthly schedule).
- Scheduled maintenance: standard 8 hours/month maintenance window carveout.
- Monthly credit cap: credits capped at 10% of that month's monthly invoice for hosted inference; for Dedicated we can discuss an alternate fixed cap.
- Remedy ladder: 99.95–99.9 = 5% credit; 99.9–99.5 = 10%; <99.5 = 30% (subject to monthly cap above).

I've attached a short draft SLA with the burst language and a CSV with tier math (SLA-draft-Edgewave-v2.pdf, redwood-sla-tiering-table.csv).

Looping in Laura and Ben for procurement and legal posture. Laura — any immediate concerns on the burst carveout language?

Best,
Vivek

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SLA-draft-Edgewave-v2.pdf, redwood-sla-tiering-table.csv
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-04T08:43:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Initial ask — SLA uptime baseline and monthly credit cap

Marissa — quick internal note. Edgewave wants a burst-tolerance carveout tied to their nightly batch windows. My thinking:

- Define "batch window" in the SLA as a recurring schedule the customer declares (cron or list of ranges).
- Allow up to 4 cumulative hours/month where degraded P95 latency doesn't count toward uptime.
- For unannounced bursts (not in the schedule), standard uptime applies.
- Keep monthly cap at 10% for hosted, but offer a reduced 6% cap if they commit to a 12-month reserved capacity (Dedicated).

Can you take a pass on how this interacts with our monitoring/tracing obligations and the remediation calculation? Also feed any legal phrasing edits — I want procurement to have a clean amendment next week.

— Vivek

Date: 2027-10-05T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Initial ask — SLA uptime baseline and monthly credit cap

Vivek — quick notes from ops/legal review:

- Operationally we can measure per-route latency and tie the batch window to a label on requests; need them to expose the window in their config (or we pull from a small webhook schedule).
- Suggest clarifying "degraded" as p95 > X ms for > 3 consecutive minutes to avoid spiky noise. Ops prefers p95 threshold over instantaneous p99 checks.
- Legal: tidy the monthly cap language to say "credits shall not exceed the lesser of (i) 10% of billed charges for the month; or (ii) USD $100,000" — gives us bounded exposure.
- If they want the reduced cap (6%), require a 12-month committed Dedicated booking and a migration plan.

I'll redline the draft and remove ambiguous phrases. Flagging Ben for procurement input on the Dedicated commitment structure.

Marissa

Marissa Cole
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Amalie Jensen <amalie.jensen@edgewave.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-07T13:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA commitment tiers & monthly credit carveouts — Edgewave negotiation

Hi Amalie — thanks for your patience. Attached is the redlined amendment that includes:

- Precise definition of "batch window" and a method to declare it (cron or webhook).
- Burst tolerance: up to 4 cumulative hours/month where p95 latency breaches the declared threshold will be excluded from monthly uptime calculations, provided requests are labeled/tagged by the customer.
- Scheduled maintenance: up to 8 hours/month carveout.
- Monthly credit cap: credits shall not exceed the lesser of (i) 10% of billed charges for the month; or (ii) USD $100,000. Alternate: a 6% cap if Edgewave signs a 12-month Dedicated commitment (details in section 4).
- Remedy ladder updated to use p95 thresholds in the calculation and a clearer proration formula.

Next steps: if this lines up with Edgewave's procurement requirements, we can issue a DocuSign link for the amendment and kickoff the dedicated capacity discussion in parallel.

Link to DocuSign preview: https://redwood.app/docusign/EDGE-1574

Attachments: SLA-draft-Edgewave-v2-redline.pdf, redwood-sla-tiering-table.csv

Best,
Vivek
